stem: The student wants to introduce the Saltmarsh Larval Census and its purpose to an audience unfamiliar with the program. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Saltmarsh Larval Census is a volunteer program based in Portugal.
• It was founded in 2009 by marine biologist Inês Carvalho.
• Volunteers set fine-mesh plankton nets at dusk in coastal estuaries.
• The program counts the larvae of crabs and other crustaceans to track how estuary populations change from year to year.
• In 2017, the program launched an offshoot, the Larval Atlas, an online map of its data.
choices: The Larval Atlas, an online map launched in 2017, displays the data that Saltmarsh Larval Census volunteers gather in coastal estuaries each year.
Founded in 2009 by marine biologist Inês Carvalho, the Saltmarsh Larval Census is a volunteer program whose members set plankton nets at dusk.
The Saltmarsh Larval Census, a volunteer program in Portugal, counts crab and other crustacean larvae to track how estuary populations change over time.
Since 2009, the Saltmarsh Larval Census has recorded yearly shifts in estuary crustacean populations, data now mapped on the Larval Atlas.
explanation: The goal has two parts: introduce the program to readers who have never heard of it, and give its purpose. Choice C does both in one sentence. The appositive 'a volunteer program in Portugal' tells a newcomer what the Census is, and 'to track how estuary populations change over time' states what it is for. It leaves out the founder, the method and the offshoot, because the goal doesn't need them.

A.why: You saw a name followed by an identifying appositive and stopped checking. But the label belongs to the Larval Atlas, the offshoot, not to the Census. The Census is mentioned only in passing, as if the reader already knows it, and its purpose never appears.

B.why: This choice survives the first test: it tells you the Census is a volunteer program. But the goal also asks for its purpose, and this sentence gives only the founding details and the method (setting nets at dusk). It never says why the volunteers count larvae. You checked 'introduce' and forgot 'and its purpose.'

D.why: This one comes close to the purpose, since it mentions recording shifts in populations. But it never says what the Census is, so it treats the program as already familiar. It also names a second unfamiliar thing, the Larval Atlas, without explaining it. That might work for an informed reader, but it fails the stated audience.

stem: The student wants to introduce the Halvorsen Shuttle Protocol to an audience unfamiliar with it, explaining what the protocol measures. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Halvorsen Shuttle Protocol is a fitness test.
• It was designed in 1994 by Norwegian exercise physiologist Erik Halvorsen.
• Athletes sprint repeatedly between two lines 20 meters apart, with rest intervals that shrink each round.
• It measures how quickly an athlete recovers between bursts of high-intensity effort.
• In 2011, a shorter version, the Mini-Halvorsen, was created for youth soccer academies.
choices: Norwegian exercise physiologist Erik Halvorsen designed the Halvorsen Shuttle Protocol in 1994, in which athletes sprint between lines 20 meters apart.
The Halvorsen Shuttle Protocol, a fitness test of repeated 20-meter sprints, measures how quickly an athlete recovers between bursts of intense effort.
The Mini-Halvorsen, a shorter fitness test created in 2011 for youth soccer academies, adapts the longer Halvorsen Shuttle Protocol.
Because its rest intervals shrink each round, the Halvorsen Shuttle Protocol reveals how quickly an athlete recovers between bursts of intense effort.
explanation: A reader who has never heard of the protocol first needs to know what it is, and the goal also asks what it measures. Choice B covers both. The appositive 'a fitness test of repeated 20-meter sprints' identifies the protocol as a type of thing, and the main clause states what it measures: recovery between bursts of high-intensity effort.

A.why: You looked for an identifying label and found one, but it's attached to the wrong noun. 'Norwegian exercise physiologist' tells you who Erik Halvorsen is, not what his protocol is. The sentence describes the sprints but never says what the protocol measures, which is the specific thing the goal asks for.

C.why: This is the subtype's trap. It gives a clear label, but to the Mini-Halvorsen, a later offshoot. It mentions the main protocol only as something already known and never says what either test measures.

D.why: This is the trap that survives the first insight. It does state what the protocol measures, so it seems to meet the goal. But it never says the protocol is a fitness test, and 'its rest intervals' and 'each round' refer to a structure the reader hasn't been told about. The sentence assumes the reader already knows what the protocol is, so it fails the stated audience.
